name: Necromancer: a mob killed by an unordered Ghoul defending its owner is lootable (#4875)
contract: npc_ascension_necromancer::IsSummonedBy set the minion's owner GUID directly instead of routing through Unit::SetMinion, so the summon never got m_ControlledByPlayer or UNIT_FLAG_PLAYER_CONTROLLED. Unit::DealDamage only counts a kill's damage toward Creature::LowerPlayerDamageReq's _playerDamageReq threshold when the attacker IsControlledByPlayer() and is owned by a player; without that flag a mob killed purely by the Ghoul's own damage never cleared the 50 percent threshold and Unit::Kill cleared its loot recipient, exactly as #4875 reports (XP sometimes arrives from incidental player damage, loot does not). This scenario never casts a Command spell (which would otherwise bypass the gate directly through Order()'s own LowerPlayerDamageReq call) and the Necromancer never attacks: the aggressive Grimtotem Marauder (mulgore-grimtotem-aggro-range.json's proven natural-aggro fixture, not civilian) engages the player on its own, and the Ghoul's own UpdateAI picks it up solely through the player->getAttackers() fallback, fights it off and kills it unordered. The fix must make that kill lootable and worth experience.

steps.label: Let spawn AI settle out of aggro range
SETUP: the Marauder leaves a distant Necromancer alone
Walk the Necromancer into the Marauder's aggro range
SETUP: the aggressive Marauder engages the Necromancer on its own
Let the Ghoul pick up the player's existing attacker unordered
SETUP: the Ghoul kills the Marauder without any Command cast
CONTROL: the Necromancer never swung at the Marauder
An unordered, minion-only kill is worth experience
The experience did not cross a level, so the delta is meaningful
The owner can open the Marauder's guaranteed copper loot despite never ordering or attacking it
The owner receives the guaranteed copper
